global_problem.statement: Least number of goods admitting a three-agent nonnegative additive real valuation profile with no complete PMMS allocation.

claims.statement: Every three-agent instance with at most eight goods and nonnegative additive valuations admits a complete PMMS allocation. No external theorem is used; The EFX existence theorem is not used.

Goelz's two nine-good instances and Bei et al.'s Table 2 instance have no PMMS allocation among all 19,683 complete allocations; deleting any one good from any of them leaves at least five PMMS allocations.

3q-1 goods: one q-balanced agent a, and a labelling {b,c} with v_c(P) <= v_c(M - P)/2 for P = b's top q-1 goods, imply a PMMS allocation (top-two / balanced cut-and-choose). Contains Theorem 6; strict (explicit instance with one balanced row).

Six-good existence: base formula with all 540 nonempty complete allocations and the first agent's goods ordered, no injected theorem; 141,035 clauses; re-derived clause by clause (exact equality); refuted, LRAT accepted by both checkers.

Seven-good existence: cases (1,1,4), (1,2,3), (2,2,2) with 4-6-good restriction lemmas, Pareto maximality, least-good selector, tie-breaks and block orders; each base.cnf independently re-derived clause by clause; each LRAT proof accepted by lrat-check and by the Python checker.
Seven-good existence, variant with the EFX lemma and own-value maximality; same checks. Not used by the proof; its certificates are not part of the published evidence package.
Perturbation lemma: a counterexample on a fixed set of goods yields a positive generic one.
Cardinality theorem for 3q-1 goods; for eight goods at least two agents of a counterexample are top-heavy.
evidence: paper/pmms8.pdf Theorem 6 (as a case of Proposition 7)

claims.statement: The normalisation of Section 3.5 is valid and its clauses hold for the canonical form of any positive generic matrix; 16 eight-good and 30 seven-good random trials exercised every size profile.

Semantic control: for random positive generic matrices at 6, 7 and 8 goods and for the Goelz projection, every non-failure clause holds and the number of violated allocation clauses equals the exact number of PMMS allocations.
Section 6: structure of hard eight-good instances; three natural statements refuted by explicit instances, each re-enumerated by a separate pure-Python implementation.
Simulated annealing over integer eight-good profiles reached one surviving PMMS allocation at zero slack repeatedly and never zero. Not used by the proof.

release_boundary: m* = 9 is supported by the published evidence: ten trimmed eight-good LRAT certificates plus the six- and seven-good certificates, each formula re-derived clause by clause. Historical priority remains bounded by the recorded search.
